Adults aged 18 or over can pay up to £20,000 into ISAs in the 2026/27 tax year, which runs from 6 April 2026 to 5 April 2027.

You can split that allowance between cash ISAs, stocks and shares ISAs, innovative finance ISAs and a Lifetime ISA. The Lifetime ISA has its own limit of £4,000. Any unused allowance does not carry forward.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

The ISA allowance for 2026/27 is £20,000 per adult aged 18 or over. The tax year runs from 6 April 2026 to 5 April 2027.

You can split the allowance between cash ISAs, stocks and shares ISAs, innovative finance ISAs and a Lifetime ISA. The Lifetime ISA has its own limit of £4,000. Any unused allowance doesn't carry forward.

More detail is in the ISA guide: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

Please ask your adviser, or call the switchboard, to find out what is available for her.

You can pay up to £4,000 a year into a Lifetime ISA. That counts towards the £20,000 overall ISA allowance. The government adds a 25% bonus of up to £1,000 a year.

You can open a Lifetime ISA if you are aged 18 to 39. Withdrawals for reasons other than those below incur a 25% government charge. The no-charge reasons are:
- buying a first home costing £450,000 or less, once the account has been open for at least 12 months
- being aged 60 or over
- being terminally ill with less than 12 months to live

More detail is in the ISAs guide: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

At 42, you're over the age limit for opening a Lifetime ISA. Our guide says they can be opened by anyone aged 18 to 39.

The £20,000 yearly ISA allowance is open to adults aged 18 or over. It can be split between cash ISAs, stocks and shares ISAs and innovative finance ISAs. If you want to know which would suit you, that's a question for an adviser. More details are in the ISA guide: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

The changes take effect from 6 April 2027:

- Investors under 65 can pay at most £12,000 a tax year into cash ISAs. The overall £20,000 ISA allowance is unchanged. The remainder can still go into stocks and shares or innovative finance ISAs. Investors aged 65 and over keep a £20,000 cash ISA limit.
- You will no longer be able to transfer from stocks and shares or innovative finance ISAs into cash ISAs.
- A charge will apply to interest paid on cash held inside a stocks and shares or innovative finance ISA.
- Money already in cash ISAs is not affected by the cap.

More detail is in the ISA guide: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

I can't advise on what you should do with your own ISAs. For that, please speak to an adviser.

The £12,000 cash ISA cap applies to investors under 65, so it doesn't apply to you at 70. From 6 April 2027, investors aged 65 and over keep a £20,000 cash ISA limit.

Money already in cash ISAs isn't affected by the cap. More details are in the ISA guide: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

Under HM Revenue & Customs' guidelines, ISA transfers should complete within 30 calendar days. Transfers between cash ISAs should take no more than 15 working days. Moving holdings as they are (re-registration in specie) can take longer if fund managers are slow to respond.

If the holdings are sold first and moved as cash, the proceeds move once the sales have settled. That is normally within four working days of dealing. The new provider starts the transfer. We don't charge for transfers in or out.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/client-support/closing-or-transferring/

Yes. Our stocks and shares ISA is flexible. Money you withdraw during a tax year can be replaced in the same tax year without using more of your allowance.

The pension annual allowance is £60,000. If the total paid into your pensions in a tax year goes over it, an annual allowance charge is normally due. The total includes employer contributions and the value of any defined benefit accrual.

- **Tapering:** For high earners the allowance tapers down to a minimum of £10,000.
- **Carry forward:** You can carry forward unused allowance from the previous three tax years. You must have been a member of a registered pension scheme in those years.
- **Money purchase annual allowance:** Once you have taken taxable income flexibly from a defined contribution pension, a £10,000 money purchase annual allowance applies to further defined contribution contributions.

More detail is in the pensions guide: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/pensions/

You can draw from a defined contribution pension from age 55. This rises to 57 from 6 April 2028. You can use flexi-access drawdown, buy an annuity, take lump sums, or combine them. Each has different tax consequences.

When you apply to access a pension, we will refer you to Pension Wise and offer to book a free guidance appointment for you. The exception is if you've already had one or have received regulated advice. I can't advise which option suits you. For that, a qualified adviser can help.

More detail: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/pensions/

Yes. If the transfer value is more than £30,000, the law requires you to take appropriate independent advice before the transfer can proceed. The advice must come from a firm with Financial Conduct Authority permission to advise on pension transfers. Fernhill Wealth holds that permission.

The Financial Conduct Authority expects advisers to start from the assumption that a transfer won't be suitable. Fernhill recommends one only where it can show the transfer is clearly in your interest. The documents don't say what the rule is for transfer values of £30,000 or less.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/pensions/

From 6 April 2027, most unused pension funds and death benefits will be included in the value of your estate for inheritance tax. Benefits passing to a spouse or civil partner, or to a registered charity, remain exempt. Dependants' scheme pensions and death-in-service benefits are outside the new rules.

Income tax is separate. If you die before 75, benefits are normally paid free of income tax, within the lump sum and death benefit allowance of £1,073,100. If you die at or after 75, the recipient pays income tax at their marginal rate.

I can't say how this applies to your own circumstances. For that, please raise it with your adviser. More detail is in the pensions guide: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/pensions/

Yes. Unused annual allowance from the previous three tax years can be carried forward, provided you were a member of a registered pension scheme in those years.

For context, the annual allowance is £60,000. It tapers down to a minimum of £10,000 for high earners.

The documents give these timings for complaints:

- If we can resolve it within three working days, we confirm that in a summary resolution letter.

- If the investigation can't be completed within eight weeks of receiving your complaint, we write to explain the delay and when we expect to respond. We also explain your right to go to the Financial Ombudsman Service without waiting.

If you're unhappy with our final response, or eight weeks pass without one, you can refer the matter free of charge to the Financial Ombudsman Service. You must do this within six months of the date of our final response. Their website is www.financial-ombudsman.org.uk, and their phone numbers are 0800 023 4567 and 0300 123 9123.

The documents say the annual exempt amount for capital gains tax is £3,000. It applies to gains on investments sold in a general investment account.

Gains above that amount on shares and funds are taxed at 18% or 24%, depending on your total taxable income. You can set losses against gains in the same year. You can also carry them forward if you report them to HMRC.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/tax/

- Dividends are tax-free within the dividend allowance of £500 a year.
- Above the allowance, dividends are taxed at 10.75% for basic-rate taxpayers, 35.75% for higher-rate taxpayers and 39.35% for additional-rate taxpayers.

This is general information, not personal advice. Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/tax/

There is no dealing charge for a Bed and ISA on our model portfolios. The documents I have don't say whether any other charges apply outside the model portfolios. Please ask your adviser about that, and about whether it suits your situation.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/tax/

Pension transfers typically take four to eight weeks. The receiving provider starts the transfer. The receiving scheme carries out the checks required by the pension transfer regulations. It may require you to take guidance from MoneyHelper if those checks raise an amber flag.

We keep you informed through the portal at each stage.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/client-support/closing-or-transferring/

The new provider starts the transfer. Once we receive their request, we act on it.

To keep the ISA's tax status, make the transfer through the new provider's transfer process. Don't withdraw the money. We don't charge for transfers in or out.

HMRC guidelines say transfers between cash ISAs should take no longer than 15 working days. Other ISA transfers should take no longer than 30 calendar days. Re-registering holdings in specie can take longer if fund managers are slow to respond.

**Discretionary management:** You agree an investment mandate and risk level with us. Our investment managers then make the day-to-day decisions within that mandate.

**Advisory management:** We recommend changes, and you decide whether to make each one.

Which one suits you depends on how involved you want to be in individual decisions. Your adviser will discuss both with you, and the choice is recorded in your suitability report. More detail is at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/services/investment-management/

Portfolios are managed to one of seven risk profiles. Profile 1 is the lowest risk and is mainly cash and short-dated bonds. Profile 7 is the highest risk and is almost entirely equities.

You agree your profile with your adviser. This uses a questionnaire and a conversation about your capacity for loss. It's reviewed at every annual review. More detail is at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/services/investment-management/

If you have a discretionary portfolio and its value falls by 10% or more since the start of a quarterly reporting period, we tell you by the end of the working day on which it happens.

You also get a quarterly valuation report on the client portal. It is published within 15 working days of each quarter end. Your investment manager can discuss any report with you.

The documents don't say whether this applies to non-discretionary portfolios. Please ask your investment manager about that.

No. Our independent custodian holds your investments through its nominee company, and legal title is registered in the nominee's name. You remain the beneficial owner.

Your holdings are identified to you in the custodian's records. They are kept separate from the firm's and the custodian's own assets under the Financial Conduct Authority's client assets rules. If the firm or the custodian failed and there were a shortfall, the Financial Services Compensation Scheme may cover eligible claims up to £85,000 per person.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/services/investment-management/

Fees are the same as for the standard portfolios. These portfolios don't carry a sustainability label under the FCA's Sustainability Disclosure Requirements.
